name: codex-orchestration
description: Two-stage classification and single-agent execution with previous-task continuity.

interface.longDescription: Activate Codex Orchestration with Turn Orchestration on, Use Orchestration, or Use Orchestration for this chat. Version 0.9.0 uses two stages only: GPT-5.6 Terra / Extra High classifies the request, then one Luna / Max, Terra / Max, or Sol / High agent owns the work. There are no supervisors, implementation checkpoints, or review loops. The selected agent interprets scope, performs the work, verifies it, completes any explicitly authorized release, and writes a complete final response with continuity, substantive current state, a legitimate next step when one exists, and a class, implementation, and root-route footer; there is no Recommendations or supervision section. Startup Git synchronization is prohibited: implementation-plus-release work checks GitHub once only after implementation and verification, deployment-only work checks when its immediate release phase begins, and work without an authorized release performs no remote Git check. Authorized deployments trace the final diff to the smallest running service set, include release jobs only when required, and verify the exact pushed revision and live path. Only the final user-facing report uses slightly less technical language for a general reader; internal routing, implementation, verification, and agent communication keep their full technical detail. Nonvisual results are relayed verbatim from the selected agent, without a root condensation pass. For experience-dependent outcomes, root performs one terminal visual check; the work summary remains primary, while a failed visual check appears only as a second Next step after the work next step. Previous-task continuity, quiet startup, premise-mismatch checks, and exact task bundles remain.
defaultPrompt: Tell me “Turn Orchestration on” for same-chat read-only, artifact, tweak, and build routing.
